content.comment_body: Is it possible for a [product_name] to work with two PT100 temperature sensors and manage a heating control valve with a 0-10V control signal? I want to monitor a feed heat control (A) around 90°C and adjust the valve (0-10V) to reach the required temperature (B), which may vary from 0-60°C. As long as the heat from (A) is sufficient, the valve should open just enough to supply the needed heat. If the temperature at (B) drops to, say, 45°C, the valve should open further, with each response happening over a set process time and monitored by the system. If (B) overshoots the target, the valve should close to prevent overheating. When the setpoint is achieved, the valve should close again.

The basic module (if equipped with analog inputs) or an [product_name] analog expansion module cannot directly process PT100/PT1000 sensors. To handle these sensors, you'll need an [product_name] RTD expansion module. For a 0-10V analog output signal, the [product_name] AQ expansion module is required.

Thanks for the clarification. I was aware of that—sorry for not stating it clearly. I plan to add the necessary modules as needed. I've read the system isn't ideal for handling both analog inputs and analog voltage outputs, but I haven’t personally encountered issues with this setup in my own projects.

analysis.insight_summary: The user asked if a [product_name] system could monitor two PT100 temperature probes and control a heating valve with a 0-10V output in a timed feedback loop. Responses clarified that the basic unit can't directly process PT100/PT1000 sensors; specific expansion modules are needed for both the sensor input and the analog output. The user is somewhat concerned about managing both analog input and output at the same time, but has not faced any problems doing so up to now.
analysis.user_expectations: User expects the [product_name] system to reliably read two PT100 sensors, process analog data for feedback control, and precisely drive a heating valve via 0-10V analog output, all integrated within a robust feedback-timed control loop.
